quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when wobbling. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, reduce speed slowly by closing the throttle, lean your weight forward and down, and get off the road as soon as possible. Avoid using the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, you should wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing so other drivers can see you. This helps with visibility during the day and at night.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid road hazards, avoid wind from other vehicles, and have an escape route. Your position should keep you out of other vehicles' blind spots and discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast you drank the alcohol
How often you usually drink alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often you usually drink alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: how much you drank, how fast you drank it, and your body weight. Your sex, health, and food intake can also matter. How often you drink does not affect BAC.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding:

options.text: The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If you feel heavy steering, leave the road immediately and check your tires.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To estimate drinks remaining, subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle:

options.text: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while sitting.
Has a seat at your waist level.
Has a seat 10 inches above your waist.
Has a seat 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while sitting.
questions.explanation: The right fit means your feet can touch the ground while you sit on the seat. Keep your feet on the footrests while riding.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, it is best to:

options.text: Have one rider pass completely before the next rider starts.
Have many riders pass at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to show no more riders are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have one rider pass completely before the next rider starts.
questions.explanation: Group riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing and return to the group formation before the next rider begins to pass.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, it is best to:

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when wobbling. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, reduce speed by slowly closing the throttle, shift your weight forward and down, and get off the road as soon as possible. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Slow down with your brakes before shifting safely.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down with your brakes before shifting safely.
questions.explanation: Before shifting to a lower gear, slow down to a safe speed. Shifting too fast can make the motorcycle lurch and the rear wheel skid. Use your brakes to reach a safe speed before downshifting.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by moving only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Bend your arms slightly when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: ______ are often painted on roads to direct riders into the proper lanes for turning.
questions.correctAnswerText: Painted white arrows
questions.explanation: White arrows painted on the pavement show you which direction to go from that lane. Follow any signs or signals along with these arrows.

questions.question: If you are approaching a hazardous location, you will likely see a sign that is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black letters.
questions.explanation: Warning signs about hazards or special conditions are yellow with black letters or symbols. Always pay attention to these warnings.

questions.question: How many crashes between motorcycles and cars are caused by the car driver failing to yield the right-of-way?
questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver did not properly yield the right-of-way to the rider.

questions.question: Impairment from drinking alcohol occurs:
questions.correctAnswerText: Well below the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Never ride a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol. Impairment starts well below the legal limit.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If you can, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride:

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front. This allows experienced riders at the back to watch over them.

questions.question: To reduce the amount of time you need to react to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces your reaction time when you need to slow down quickly.

questions.question: If you are being chased by a dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it calmly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use abrupt pressure on the front brake to prevent locking the front tire.
Use either brake, but use only one brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.
